\begin{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عزز} (ʿazzaza)}{عزز (ʿazzaza)}]{\ar{عزز} (ʿazzaza) — to strengthen}

\label{lesson:AR-C418-azzaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to become evident, then the Arabic for to refer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عزز}}
\textbf{\ar{عزز}} — \emph{ʿazzaza} — \textquotedblleft{}to strengthen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عززت} \ar{الرياضة} \ar{ثقته} \ar{بنفسه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿazzazat ar-riyāḍa thiqatahu bi-nafsih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sport strengthened his self-confidence.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعزز}, \emph{yuʿazziz}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عزز}} (\emph{ʿazzaza}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-z-z}, \textquotedblleft{}to be strong, mighty\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to make strong: to strengthen, to reinforce.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿazzaza}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿazzaza}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿazzazat ar-riyāḍa thiqatahu bi-nafsih.} — Sport strengthened his self-confidence.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to become evident, then the Arabic for to refer, then say \emph{ʿazzaza} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عزز} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To strengthen\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أضعف} (aḍʿafa)}{أضعف (aḍʿafa)}]{\ar{أضعف} (aḍʿafa) — to weaken}

\label{lesson:AR-C418-adafa-weaken}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to refer, then the Arabic for to strengthen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أضعف}}
\textbf{\ar{أضعف}} — \emph{aḍʿafa} — \textquotedblleft{}to weaken\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أضعفت} \ar{الحمى} \ar{جسمه}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aḍʿafat al-ḥummā jismah.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fever weakened his body.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يضعف}, \emph{yuḍʿif}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أضعف}} (\emph{aḍʿafa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-ʿ-f}, \textquotedblleft{}to be weak; to double\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV, to make weak: to weaken. \ar{ضعيف}, weak, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{طور} (ṭawwara)}{طور (ṭawwara)}]{\ar{طور} (ṭawwara) — to develop}

\label{lesson:AR-C418-tawwara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to strengthen, then the Arabic for to weaken.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{طور}}
\textbf{\ar{طور}} — \emph{ṭawwara} — \textquotedblleft{}to develop\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طور} \ar{المهندس} \ar{برنامجا} \ar{جديدا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭawwara al-muhandis barnāmajan jadīdan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The engineer developed a new program.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يطور}, \emph{yuṭawwir}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{طور}} (\emph{ṭawwara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṭ-w-r}, \textquotedblleft{}a time, a stage\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to move a thing on from stage to stage: to develop.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فعالية} (faʿʿāliyya)}{فعالية (faʿʿāliyya)}]{\ar{فعالية} (faʿʿāliyya) — effectiveness}

\label{lesson:AR-C418-faaliyya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to weaken, then the Arabic for to develop.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فعالية}}
\textbf{\ar{فعالية}} — \emph{faʿʿāliyya} — \textquotedblleft{}effectiveness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أثبتت} \ar{الدراسة} \ar{فعالية} \ar{الدواء}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{athbatat ad-dirāsa faʿʿāliyyat ad-dawāʾ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The study proved the effectiveness of the medicine.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فعالية}} (\emph{faʿʿāliyya}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-ʿ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to do, to act\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Faʿʿāliyya} is a modern abstract noun from \emph{faʿʿāl}, very active: effectiveness.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{faʿʿāliyya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{athbatat ad-dirāsa faʿʿāliyyat ad-dawāʾ.} — The study proved the effectiveness of the medicine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to weaken, then the Arabic for to develop, then say \emph{faʿʿāliyya} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مستقل} (mustaqill)}{مستقل (mustaqill)}]{\ar{مستقل} (mustaqill) — independent}

\label{lesson:AR-C418-mustaqill}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to develop, then the Arabic for effectiveness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مستقل}}
\textbf{\ar{مستقل}} — \emph{mustaqill} — \textquotedblleft{}independent\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أصبح} \ar{أخي} \ar{مستقلا} \ar{عن} \ar{أسرته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{aṣbaḥa akhī mustaqillan ʿan usratih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother became independent of his family.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مستقل}} (\emph{mustaqill}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{q-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be few; to lift\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives Form X for one who manages his affairs by himself alone; \emph{mustaqill}, its active participle, is independent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaqill}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mustaqill}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṣbaḥa akhī mustaqillan ʿan usratih.} — My brother became independent of his family.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to develop, then the Arabic for effectiveness, then say \emph{mustaqill} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{مستقل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Independent\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
